reasoning: The proposal's exact problem, method, and metric are already published. "Analysing the Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors" (arXiv:2603.24543) uses Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) steering vectors for benign behaviors on multiple 7B models (Llama-2-7B, Gemma-7B, Qwen-7B), fixes JailbreakBench prompts, measures ΔSR = steered ASR minus baseline ASR, and explicitly ranks vectors by induced jailbreak risk via cosine similarity to the refusal direction — which is precisely the proposed "JailbreakDelta" measurement. "Steering Externalities" (arXiv:2602.04896) independently establishes the same phenomenon (benign steering raising ASR to >80%). The only thin differentiator is packaging the metric as a turnkey tool, but the measurement methodology, ΔASR metric, ranking, models, and datasets all match the proposal directly, leaving no substantive unexplored gap.

evidence.title: Analysing the Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors
evidence.summary: Systematic safety audit of CAA steering vectors for benign behaviors across Llama-2-7B, Gemma-7B, Qwen (3B-32B). Measures ΔSR (steered ASR minus baseline at m=0) on JailbreakBench, reports up to 57% ASR increase / 50% decrease, and ranks vectors by induced jailbreak risk using cosine similarity to the refusal direction (R²>=0.85). This is essentially the proposed JailbreakDelta measurement and ranking, already implemented.

evidence.title: Steering Externalities: Benign Activation Steering Unintentionally Increases Jailbreak Risk for Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Establishes that steering vectors derived from entirely benign datasets (e.g., compliance, JSON formatting) erode safety guardrails, acting as a force multiplier that raises jailbreak ASR to over 80%. Directly addresses the proposal's core research question that benign steering changes jailbreak ASR as a side effect.

evidence.title: Minimizing Collateral Damage in Activation Steering
evidence.summary: Related follow-up work on the safety/utility trade-off and collateral effects (false refusals, safety perturbations) of activation steering, indicating an active and maturing literature around exactly the side-effect-measurement problem the proposal targets.

evidence.title: The Rogue Scalpel: Activation Steering Compromises LLM Safety
evidence.summary: Shows activation steering compromises LLM safety and creates jailbreak vulnerabilities, reinforcing that the problem of steering-induced jailbreak risk is well-covered in published work.
